title: CEO Interview with Eric Tsai of Mivium
gist: Mivium CEO Eric Tsai pitches a US-based, upstream play in GaN: phase-pure submicron GaN powder (300 to 500 nm) with third-party characterization, aimed at crystal growth, substrate and thin-film teams. The company has raised over $10.5 million, calls the powder its only product today, and treats thin films as early R&D.

insights.claim: Mivium argues that most GaN discussion centers on devices, fabs and winners in power and RF, while the starting source material gets little attention even though every GaN wafer, film and device begins there.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Upstream materials supply is an under-covered part of the GaN chain.
insights.quote: Mivium makes the starting material for GaN.

insights.claim: Demand from AI power, EVs and RF is pulling hard on everything upstream, making a controlled, repeatable GaN feedstock with real data useful to crystal growth, substrate and thin-film teams.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: End-market pull is cited as the reason for feedstock demand.

insights.claim: Mivium's announced material is phase-pure hexagonal wurtzite GaN in a 300 to 500 nanometer range, with uniform distribution and faceted morphology, characterized independently via SEM, EDS, XRD, XPS, GDMS and ICP-MS.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Third-party data addresses a standard buyer objection in materials.

insights.claim: CTO Chandra Deshpandey frames that submicron size alone is not the point; the achievement is reaching it with phase purity and uniformity meeting semiconductor-grade requirements.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Quality metrics, not particle size, define a viable feedstock.

insights.claim: Mivium says powder is the only product it can discuss today and that everything downstream is R&D; it is not a wafer or device company and does not assume its powder drops into every epitaxy flow.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Honest scoping signals early commercial stage with application-specific fit.
insights.quote: Powder is the product we can talk about today.

insights.claim: Customers' main worries are repeatability and supply: batch-to-batch behavior and scale-up reliability, with data from labs they trust rather than only the vendor.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Qualification cycles and supply assurance gate adoption of new materials.
insights.locator: What keeps the teams you talk to up at night?

insights.claim: Mivium has completed initial in-house GaN thin-film deposition derived from the powder platform, which Tsai describes as early-stage R&D extending toward semiconductor and photonics applications.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A roadmap option, not yet a product.
insights.quote: It is early-stage R&D and we describe it that way.
insights.locator: What new technology are you working on?

insights.claim: The company is US-based in Fremont, has raised more than $10.5 million, and says its platform extends to other wide bandgap materials including gallium oxide and boron nitride.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Small funding base; platform breadth is claimed rather than shown.

insights.claim: Tsai says the useful comparison is not with device makers but with whatever source material a team uses today, measured in their own workflow.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Competition is incumbent feedstock, so evaluation samples are the sales motion.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like
